teaching.hint: When does an earlier index make a possible left endpoint unnecessary?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Only strict prefix minima need be left endpoints; processing right endpoints backward finalizes each candidate at its farthest feasible match.
solution_outline.approach: Collect indices at new strict prefix minima in a stack. Scan right indices from the end, popping every candidate whose value is no greater than the current value and recording its width when the right index is larger.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The stack’s indices increase and values strictly decrease. Before a reverse-scan step, its candidates have not matched any previously scanned, farther-right endpoint.
solution_outline.correctness: A nonminimum start is dominated by an earlier no-larger value, which makes every corresponding ramp wider. For a surviving candidate, its first compatible reverse-scan endpoint is its largest possible right endpoint, so later endpoints cannot improve its width. If the smallest-valued stack top fails, all deeper candidates fail too. Thus every potentially optimal start is finalized at its best width; self-matches contribute only the zero default, not a strict ramp.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; each candidate is pushed and popped at most once.
solution_outline.pitfall: Equality is allowed when matching endpoints, while equal prefix values need not create a new candidate.

common_wrong_turns: Equality is allowed when matching endpoints, while equal prefix values need not create a new candidate.
source_fidelity_notes: Preserved strict index order and nonstrict value order; proof distinguishes zero-width self-matches from actual ramps.
